instructions: Roast 2kg red bell peppers and 1 large eggplant until skins blackened. Peel, deseed peppers, scoop eggplant flesh. Drain in colander 30 min. Finely chop or coarsely blend vegetables. In large pot, cook mixture with 2 minced garlic cloves, 2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, salt, and 1/2 cup olive oil over low heat, stirring frequently, until thickened and spreadable, about 1-1.5 hours. Add chopped chili for spicy version. Jar and seal, or refrigerate. Serbian roasted pepper relish.

name: Knedlíky
instructions: Make yeast dough: dissolve 1 packet yeast in 1/2 cup warm milk with pinch sugar. Mix 3 cups flour, 1 tsp salt, 1 egg, yeasted milk, enough additional milk to make soft dough. Knead until smooth. Let rise 1 hour. Punch down, knead in 1 cup toasted bread cubes and chopped parsley. Shape into 2 logs. Boil large pot salted water, carefully add dumplings, simmer covered 20-25 min. Remove, slice with thread or sharp knife. Serve as side with goulash or roast pork. Czech bread dumplings.

name: Flaki
instructions: Clean and precook tripe as for ciorbă. Cut into thin strips. In beef broth, cook tripe with julienned carrot, parsley root, celery, sautéed onion until tripe tender, 2-3 hours. Season generously with marjoram, sweet paprika, pinch ginger and nutmeg, salt and pepper. Thicken with roux if desired. Serve hot with fresh parsley and bread. Traditional Polish tripe soup.

name: Sarmale
instructions: Rinse sour cabbage leaves if too salty. Mix 300g ground pork, 200g ground beef, 1/2 cup uncooked rice, sautéed onion, chopped dill, thyme, salt, pepper. Place spoonful on each leaf, roll tightly tucking ends. Line pot with chopped cabbage and smoked bacon. Pack sarmale tightly. Mix 2 cups water with 2 tbsp tomato paste, pour over. Top with more bacon and bay leaves. Cover, simmer 2-2.5 hours. Serve hot with sour cream and polenta (mămăligă). Romanian stuffed cabbage rolls.

name: Zapiekanka
instructions: Slice baguette lengthwise, toast lightly. Sauté sliced mushrooms and onion until soft, season. Spread toasted bread with ketchup. Top with mushroom mixture, diced ham if using, generous grated cheese (gouda or mozzarella). Bake at 200°C (400°F) until cheese melted and bubbly, 8-10 min. Remove, drizzle with mayonnaise, sprinkle with chopped chives. Polish street food open-faced sandwich.

name: Kibinai
instructions: Make pastry: cut 200g cold butter into 3 cups flour with salt. Add 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 egg, knead until smooth. Chill. For filling: finely chop 300g lamb and 200g pork (or use ground), mix with 1 finely chopped onion, 2-3 tbsp broth, salt, pepper, caraway seeds. Roll dough, cut circles. Place filling, fold into half-moon, crimp edges decoratively. Bake at 200°C (400°F) 20-25 min until golden. Lithuanian Karaite meat pastries.

name: Mămăligă
instructions: Bring 4 cups water to boil with 1 tsp salt. Slowly pour 1.5 cups coarse cornmeal in thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce heat to low, cook stirring frequently with wooden spoon until very thick and pulls away from sides, about 20-25 min. Turn out onto wooden board. Slice with string. Serve hot with butter, sour cream, grated cheese, and fried eggs. Romanian polenta, staple side dish.

name: Sild Med Karrysalat
instructions: Drain pickled herring fillets, cut into bite-sized pieces. Finely dice 1 onion and 1 crisp apple. Mix 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp yogurt, 1 tsp curry powder, pinch turmeric, lemon juice, salt, pepper. Fold in herring, onion, apple. Let marinate 1 hour. Serve on buttered dark rye bread, topped with chives. Danish curried herring salad.

name: Okroshka
instructions: Boil 3 potatoes and 3 eggs, cool, peel, dice. Finely chop 2 cucumbers, 5 radishes, bunch green onions, and fresh dill. Dice 200g cooked sausage or ham. Mix all in large bowl. For dressing: whisk 1L kefir (or kvass) with 2 tbsp sour cream, 1 tsp mustard, salt. Pour over vegetables, stir. Chill thoroughly. Serve cold, garnished with extra dill and halved boiled egg. Russian summer cold soup.

name: Pirozhki
instructions: Prepare yeast dough: 3 cups flour, 1 cup warm milk, 1 egg, 2 tbsp butter, 1 tsp yeast, sugar, salt. Let rise 1 hour. For filling: sauté onion, add ground beef, cook until done. Mix with cooked rice, chopped hard-boiled egg, dill, salt, pepper. Or make cabbage filling with sautéed shredded cabbage and onion. Roll dough, cut circles, place filling, seal into oval shape. Let rise 20 min. Brush with egg wash, bake at 180°C (350°F) 20-25 min until golden, or fry in oil. Russian hand pies.

name: Sbiten
instructions: Dissolve 1/2 cup honey in 4 cups hot water. Add 3 tbsp berry jam (raspberry or cherry), 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 2 cardamom pods, slice of fresh ginger. Simmer gently 15-20 min, do not boil. Turn off heat, add fresh mint leaves and slice of lemon. Let steep 10 min. Strain, serve hot. Traditional Russian honey-based winter drink, often with medicinal herbs.

name: Pampushky
instructions: Make yeast dough: 2.5 cups flour, 1/2 cup warm milk, 1 egg, 2 tbsp sugar, pinch salt, 1 tsp yeast, 30g melted butter. Knead, rise 1 hour. Form small round buns, place in greased pan close together. Let rise 20 min. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 20 min. Meanwhile, mix 2 tbsp oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped dill and parsley. Brush hot pampushky with garlic mixture. Serve with borscht. Ukrainian garlic rolls.

name: Lazy Cabbage Rolls
instructions: Finely shred 1/2 head cabbage, blanch 5 min, drain. Sauté chopped onion and grated carrot. Mix 500g ground beef with 1/2 cup cooked rice, cabbage, sautéed vegetables, salt, pepper. Form into oval patties. Brown in skillet. Place in pot, pour mixture of 1 cup broth, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp sour cream. Simmer covered 30 min. Serve with sour cream and dill. Easier version of golubtsy.

name: Kasha
instructions: Rinse 1 cup buckwheat. Bring 2 cups water to boil with pinch salt, add buckwheat, reduce heat to low, cover, cook 15-20 min until liquid absorbed. Turn off heat, let stand covered 10 min. Fluff with fork, add butter. For savory version: sauté sliced mushrooms and onion in butter, mix with cooked kasha. For breakfast: serve with milk, butter, and sugar. Traditional Russian porridge, staple food.

name: Tvorog Zapekanka
instructions: Mix 500g farmer's cheese with 2 eggs, 1/3 cup sugar, 3 tbsp semolina, 2 tbsp sour cream, 1 tsp vanilla, and handful raisins. Let stand 15 min for semolina to swell. Grease baking dish with butter, sprinkle with breadcrumbs. Pour mixture, smooth top. Dot with small butter pieces. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 35-40 min until golden and set. Serve warm with sour cream, jam, or honey. Russian cheese pudding/casserole.

name: Rassolnik
instructions: Cook 1/4 cup pearl barley separately. Sauté diced onion and carrot, add 1 tbsp tomato paste. Bring 2L broth to boil, add diced potatoes, cook 10 min. Add sautéed vegetables, barley, 2 sliced pickles, 1/2 cup pickle brine, bay leaf. Simmer 15 min. Season with salt if needed. Serve with sour cream and fresh dill. Traditional Russian soup with pickles.

name: Medovik
instructions: For cake layers: melt 100g butter with 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup sugar over double boiler. Add 1 tsp baking soda, mixture will foam. Remove from heat, cool slightly, add 3 eggs, then 2.5-3 cups flour. Knead soft dough. Divide into 8-10 pieces, roll very thin, bake at 180°C (350°F) 3-4 min each until golden. Trim edges, save crumbs. For cream: whip 500g sour cream with 1 cup powdered sugar and 1 cup heavy cream until thick. Layer cakes with cream, covering entire cake. Sprinkle with reserved cake crumbs. Refrigerate overnight. Russian honey cake.

name: Pryaniki
instructions: Heat 1/2 cup honey with 1/2 cup sugar and 100g butter until dissolved, cool. Add 2 eggs, 1 tsp spice mix (cinnamon, ginger, cardamom, cloves), 2.5 cups flour, 1 tsp baking powder. Knead dough, rest 1 hour. Roll out 1 cm thick, cut shapes. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 12-15 min. Make glaze: mix powdered sugar with lemon juice or milk. Glaze warm cookies. Let dry. Russian spice cookies.

name: Holodnik
instructions: Boil beet tops or sorrel in small amount water until wilted, cool in broth. Grate 2 cucumbers, slice radishes, chop green onions and dill. Mix with 1L cold kefir, add cooled beet broth for pink color. Season with salt. Serve with halved hard-boiled egg and hot boiled potato on side. Belarusian cold summer soup, similar to šaltibarščiai but with sorrel.

name: Mochi
ingredients: red bean paste or ice cream filling
instructions: Mix 1 cup glutinous rice flour with 1/4 cup sugar and 1 cup water. Steam or microwave covered until translucent and stretchy. Dust surface with cornstarch, turn out hot dough, knead briefly with cornstarch to prevent sticking. Divide into portions, flatten, wrap around filling (sweet red bean paste or small scoop ice cream). Seal well. For ice cream mochi, freeze until firm. Japanese confection, included for variety while staying in Asia/Europe theme.

name: Hünkar Beğendi
instructions: Make lamb stew: brown cubed lamb, sauté onion, pepper, tomato, tomato paste, add water, simmer until tender. For beğendi: roast 2 eggplants until soft, peel, mash. Melt 3 tbsp butter, add 3 tbsp flour, cook 1 min. Gradually whisk in 2 cups warm milk until smooth. Add mashed eggplant, salt, pepper, grated cheese. Cook until thick. Serve lamb stew over eggplant puree. Turkish 'Sultan's Delight'.

name: Manti (Turkish)
instructions: Make dough as for pelmeni, rest. Finely chop onion, mix with ground lamb, salt, pepper. Roll dough very thin, cut into small squares (2-3 cm). Place tiny amount filling, fold into small manti shapes (Turkish style are tiny). Boil in salted water or steam. For sauce: mix yogurt with crushed garlic and salt. Make paprika butter by melting butter with paprika. Serve manti topped with yogurt sauce, drizzle of paprika butter, sprinkle sumac and dried mint. Turkish dumplings.

name: Fasulye
instructions: Sauté 1 chopped onion in olive oil until soft. Add minced garlic, cook 1 min. Add 500g trimmed green beans, 2 chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato paste, pinch sugar, salt, 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer until beans tender, 30-40 min. Serve warm or cold with squeeze of lemon. Turkish olive oil braised green beans.

name: Cacik
instructions: Grate 1 cucumber, squeeze out excess liquid. Mix 2 cups thick yogurt with 1/2 cup cold water, whisk until smooth. Add cucumber, 1-2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped dill and mint, salt, drizzle of olive oil. Chill. Serve as cold soup or dip. Turkish cucumber yogurt.

name: Gözleme
instructions: Make soft dough: 2 cups flour, 1/2 cup warm water, pinch yeast, salt, oil. Knead, rest 30 min. Divide into balls, roll very thin into circles. For filling: mix chopped spinach with crumbled feta and sautéed onion (or use seasoned minced meat). Place filling on half, fold over, seal edges. Cook on hot griddle without oil, flipping until golden spots appear and filling hot. Brush with butter before serving. Turkish flatbread.

name: Kunefe
instructions: Make syrup: boil 1.5 cups sugar with 1 cup water and squeeze lemon, simmer 10 min, cool. Shred kadayif, mix with melted butter. Press half into pan, layer with cheese (like mozzarella or akkawi), top with remaining kadayif. Cook over medium heat until bottom golden, flip using plate, cook other side. Pour cooled syrup over hot künefe. Top with ground pistachios. Serve warm. Turkish cheese dessert.

name: Imam Bayildi
instructions: Cut slits in small eggplants, soak in salt water, pat dry. Sauté sliced onions and peppers in generous olive oil. Add chopped tomato, garlic, parsley, sugar, salt. Stuff mixture into eggplant slits. Place in baking dish, drizzle with olive oil and little water. Cover, bake at 180°C (350°F) 45-50 min until eggplant soft. Serve warm or room temp. Turkish stuffed eggplant, 'the imam fainted'.

name: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
instructions: Dice 2 tomatoes, 1 cucumber, 1 bell pepper. Thinly slice 1 small onion. Chop parsley. Toss vegetables with olive oil, vinegar, salt. Generously grate sirene cheese over top. Do not mix cheese in. Serve as starter. Traditional Bulgarian salad.

name: Banitsa
instructions: Mix 4 eggs, 1 cup yogurt, 200g crumbled sirene cheese, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/4 cup oil. Layer 5 phyllo sheets in greased pan, brushing each with butter. Spread some filling. Repeat layers, ending with phyllo. Cut into squares. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 40-45 min until golden and puffed. Let cool slightly. Bulgarian cheese pie, often eaten for breakfast.

name: Tarator
instructions: Whisk 2 cups yogurt with 2 cups cold water. Grate 1 cucumber, squeeze. Add cucumber, 1 crushed garlic clove, chopped dill, 1/4 cup chopped walnuts, salt, olive oil. Chill well. Serve as cold soup in summer. Bulgarian version of cacik, with walnuts.

name: Kiflice
instructions: Make yeast dough as for rolls. Roll thin, cut into triangles. Place small spoonful jam or cheese at wide end, roll toward point to form crescent. Curve slightly. Brush with egg wash, sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 15-20 min until golden. Serbian crescent rolls.

name: Prebranac
instructions: Soak 500g white beans overnight. Drain, boil with bay leaf until just tender. Drain, reserve liquid. Caramelize 3 sliced onions in oil until deep golden. Mix beans with onions, sweet paprika, crushed garlic, salt, pepper. Place in baking dish, add enough bean liquid to just cover. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 45-60 min until top browned and creamy. Serbian baked beans.

name: Kohuke
instructions: Mix 250g farmer's cheese with 2 tbsp softened butter, 2 tbsp sugar, vanilla until smooth. Form into small bars, making indentation for filling. Add teaspoon jam or dulce de leche, cover with cheese mixture. Chill. Melt chocolate, coat each bar. Refrigerate until set. Estonian glazed cheese curd snack.

name: Ćevapi
instructions: Mix 300g ground beef and 200g ground lamb with 1 finely grated onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp paprika, salt, pepper. Knead thoroughly, cover and refrigerate overnight. Shape into small finger-sized sausages. Grill over hot coals or in cast iron pan until charred and cooked through, about 6-8 min. Serve tucked into warm somun flatbread with chopped raw onion, ajvar, and kajmak (clotted cream). Traditional Balkan skinless sausages.

name: Pljeskavica
instructions: Combine 400g ground beef and 100g ground pork with 1 finely chopped onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp baking soda, salt, pepper. Add splash of carbonated mineral water for juiciness. Knead well, refrigerate 2 hours. Form into large thin patties (1.5 cm thick). Grill over high heat until charred outside, juicy inside, 4-5 min per side. Serve in warm lepinja bread with kajmak and urnebes (spicy cheese salad). Serbian style burger patty.

name: Khinkali
instructions: Make stiff dough from 3 cups flour, 1 cup water, pinch salt. Knead well, rest 1 hour. Mix 300g ground beef, 200g ground pork, 1 finely chopped onion, 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, 1 tsp cumin, chili flakes, salt, generous black pepper. Add 1/4 cup cold broth or water to make juicy filling. Roll dough thin, cut 10cm circles. Place spoonful filling, pleat edges gathering upwards to form pouch with top knot (traditionally 18-28 pleats). Pinch firmly. Boil in salted water until they float, then 7-8 min more. Serve hot, sprinkled with black pepper. Eat by holding knot, biting small hole, sipping broth, then eating rest. Georgian dumplings.

name: Chakhokhbili
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in butter until golden, remove. Sauté 3 sliced onions in same pot until soft and golden. Add 4-5 chopped fresh tomatoes (or 1 can tomatoes), cook 10 min until saucy. Return chicken, add 1 tbsp khmeli suneli (Georgian spice blend), 1 tsp ground coriander, minced garlic, chopped chili. Simmer covered 30-35 min until chicken tender and sauce thickened. At end, stir in generous amounts of chopped cilantro, basil, parsley, and squeeze of lemon juice. Serve with fresh bread or potatoes. Georgian chicken stew with herbs.

name: Lobio
instructions: Soak 300g red beans overnight, boil until tender. Drain, reserve liquid. Sauté finely chopped onion until golden. Crush 1/2 cup walnuts with garlic, coriander, fenugreek, chili, salt. Mix beans with onion, walnut paste, chopped cilantro. Add enough bean liquid to make thick stew. Simmer 10 min, add splash of vinegar. Serve warm or cold, garnished with pomegranate seeds and fresh cilantro. Georgian bean dish.

name: Chkmeruli
instructions: Butterfly whole chicken, season with salt, pepper, coriander. Pan-fry skin side down in butter until golden and crisp, flip and cook other side. Meanwhile, make garlic sauce: crush 6-8 garlic cloves, mix with 1/2 cup milk and 1/2 cup water, pinch salt. When chicken is almost done, pour garlic sauce into pan around chicken. Bring to simmer, cover and cook 10 min until chicken cooked and sauce creamy. Sprinkle with chili flakes. Serve with bread to soak up sauce. Georgian garlic chicken.

name: Ajapsandali
instructions: Cube eggplant, salt, let drain. Cube potatoes, parboil. Sauté onion, garlic, bell pepper in oil. Add eggplant, cook until soft. Add tomatoes, potatoes, khmeli suneli, chili, salt. Simmer until vegetables tender and stew thick, about 20 min. Stir in loads of fresh herbs: cilantro, basil, parsley. Serve warm or room temp as side or main. Georgian vegetable stew.

name: Lagman
instructions: Make dough from 3 cups flour, 1 cup water, 1 egg, salt. Knead, rest, roll and cut into thick noodles or pull into long strands. For sauce: brown meat chunks, add sliced onion, carrot, bell pepper, tomato, garlic, spices, cook 5 min. Add water to cover, simmer 1.5 hours until meat tender. Add diced potato and radish, cook until soft. Boil noodles separately. Serve noodles in bowl, topped with meat and vegetable sauce, sprinkle with cilantro. Central Asian hand-pulled noodle soup.

name: Shurpa
instructions: In large pot, brown lamb chunks with bone. Cover with cold water, bring to boil, skim foam. Add whole onion, carrot, bay leaf, simmer 1.5 hours. Add soaked chickpeas, cook 30 min. Add diced potatoes, turnip, bell pepper, tomatoes, cumin, coriander. Simmer until vegetables tender. Season with salt. Serve in bowls, sprinkle with fresh dill, parsley, cilantro. Hearty Central Asian soup.

name: Dolma
instructions: Rinse preserved grape leaves, blanch if fresh. Mix 300g ground lamb, 1/2 cup uncooked rice, 1 finely chopped onion, 1/4 cup each chopped dill, mint, parsley, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, salt, pepper. Place spoonful on leaf, roll tightly tucking sides. Line pot with extra leaves, pack dolma snugly. Add water to just cover, weight with plate. Simmer gently 45-50 min until rice cooked. Serve warm or room temp with yogurt garlic sauce and lemon wedges. Stuffed grape leaves.

name: Svíčková
instructions: Lard beef roast with bacon strips, sear on all sides. Remove, sauté diced onion, carrot, celery root, parsley root. Add roast back, cover with water, add lemon zest, bay leaf, allspice, thyme. Braise in oven at 160°C (320°F) for 2-2.5 hours until tender. Remove roast, strain and puree vegetables with some liquid. Return puree to pot, thicken with roux or heavy cream, add splash vinegar and sugar to balance. Slice beef, serve with creamy vegetable sauce, cranberry preserve, lemon slice, and bread dumplings (knedlíky). Czech national dish.

name: Žurek
instructions: Make sour rye starter: mix 1/2 cup rye flour with 1 cup water, add crust of rye bread, garlic clove. Let ferment 3-5 days. For soup: sauté chopped bacon and onion. Add 6 cups water or broth, diced potatoes, bay leaf, allspice. When potatoes tender, whisk in 1-2 cups rye starter, simmer 10 min. Add sliced white sausage, marjoram, salt, pepper. Finish with sour cream off heat. Serve in bread bowl or with hard-boiled egg. Polish sour rye soup.

name: Kopytka
instructions: Boil 1kg potatoes in skins, peel while warm, mash or rice. Cool slightly. Mix with 1 egg, pinch salt, and about 1.5-2 cups flour to form soft dough. Roll into ropes, flatten slightly, cut diagonally into 'hoof' shapes. Boil in salted water until they float, then 2-3 min more. Drain. Sauté breadcrumbs in butter, toss kopytka in mixture. Alternatively, serve with fried bacon and caramelized onion. Polish potato dumplings.

name: Lángos
instructions: Make yeast dough with 2 cups flour, 1/2 cup mashed potato, 1/2 cup milk, 1 tsp yeast, salt. Knead, rise 1 hour. Divide dough, stretch into flat rounds. Deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden. Rub hot lángos with cut garlic clove. Top with sour cream and grated cheese (trappista). Also popular with garlic oil only. Hungarian fried bread.

name: Paprikás Csirke
instructions: Sauté chopped onion in lard until translucent. Remove from heat, stir in 2 tbsp sweet Hungarian paprika (to prevent burning). Return to heat, add chicken pieces, brown. Add chopped tomato and bell pepper, salt, small amount water. Cover, simmer until chicken tender, about 40 min. Remove chicken, whisk 1/2 cup sour cream with 1 tbsp flour, stir into sauce. Return chicken, warm through. Serve with nokedli (small egg dumplings) or pasta. Hungarian chicken paprikash.

name: Töltött Káposzta
instructions: Mix 500g ground pork with 1/2 cup cooked rice, sautéed onion, 1 tsp paprika, salt, pepper. Rinse sour cabbage leaves, reserve juice. Roll filling in leaves, tuck ends. Line pot with chopped cabbage and smoked sausage slices. Arrange rolls, add bay leaf, tomato paste mixed with water and some cabbage juice. Simmer covered 2 hours. Thicken sauce with roux if desired. Serve with sour cream. Hungarian stuffed cabbage.

name: Vanilkové Rohlíčky
instructions: Mix 2 cups flour, 1 cup cold butter, 1/2 cup ground walnuts, 1/2 cup sugar, 1 packet vanilla sugar, 2 egg yolks into dough. Chill 1 hour. Form small crescent shapes. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 12-15 min until lightly golden. While warm, roll in powdered sugar mixed with vanilla sugar. Czech vanilla crescents, traditional Christmas cookie.

name: Burek sa Mesom
instructions: Sauté finely chopped onion and garlic, add ground beef, brown. Season with paprika, salt, pepper. Drain excess fat. Grease round baking pan. Layer phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil mixture, occasionally sprinkling with meat mixture. When half sheets used, add more meat, then remaining phyllo. Cut into spiral or slices before baking. Mix oil with sparkling water, pour over top. Bake at 200°C (400°F) 35-40 min until golden. Let rest, serve with yogurt. Bosnian meat pie.

name: Ikra (Baklazhannaya)
instructions: Roast 2 eggplants and 2 bell peppers until skins charred, peel, chop. Sauté finely chopped onion and grated carrot until soft. Add chopped tomatoes, cook 10 min. Add chopped roasted vegetables, minced garlic, 1 tbsp tomato paste, splash vinegar, pinch sugar, salt, pepper. Simmer 20-30 min until thick, stirring often. Cool. Serve as spread on bread. Russian/Eastern European eggplant 'caviar'.

name: Ostri (Moravian Sparrow)
instructions: Cut pork into cubes, season. Brown in batches, remove. Sauté chopped onion with caraway seeds, add minced garlic and paprika. Return meat, add broth to almost cover, simmer covered 1.5 hours until tender. Thicken juices with flour slurry. Serve with bread dumplings and stewed sauerkraut. Czech 'Moravian Sparrow' (pork stew).

name: Käsekrainer
instructions: Prick cheese-filled sausages (Käsekrainer) to prevent bursting. Grill or pan-fry until crisp and cheese melting inside. Slice diagonally. Serve in sliced bread roll with mustard, horseradish, and sprinkle of curry powder. Popular Austrian street food sausage.

name: Frikadeller
instructions: Mix 300g ground pork, 200g ground veal, 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 1/2 cup milk, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, salt, pepper. Form into oval patties. Pan-fry in butter until golden and cooked through. Serve with boiled potatoes, brown gravy, and lingonberry jam. Danish meatballs.

name: Smørrebrød
instructions: Slice dense Danish rye bread (rugbrød), spread generously with butter. Create open-faced sandwiches with various toppings. Classic combinations: pickled herring with onion rings and dill; roast beef with remoulade, crispy fried onions, and horseradish; shrimp with lemon, mayo, and dill; liver pâté with bacon and pickled beets. Arrange artfully. Danish open sandwich.

name: Gravlax
instructions: Mix equal parts salt and sugar (about 1/4 cup each) with 1 tbsp crushed white pepper. Place salmon fillet skin-side down on plastic wrap. Generously coat flesh with mixture, top with lots of fresh dill. Wrap tightly, place in dish, weight with cans. Refrigerate 2-3 days, turning every 12 hours. Unwrap, scrape off salt mixture, pat dry. Slice thinly. Serve with mustard dill sauce (hovmästarsås) on rye bread or with boiled potatoes. Swedish cured salmon.

name: Köttbullar
instructions: Mix 250g ground beef, 250g ground pork, 1 finely chopped sautéed onion, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs soaked in 1/4 cup milk, 1 egg, 1/2 tsp allspice, pinch nutmeg, salt, pepper. Form small round meatballs. Fry in butter until browned and cooked. Make cream sauce in same pan with flour, beef broth, and cream. Serve meatballs with sauce, mashed potatoes, lingonberry jam, and pickled cucumber. Swedish meatballs.

name: Túrós Csusza
instructions: Cook 300g square pasta (csusza) in salted water until al dente. Meanwhile, dice 150g bacon and fry until crisp. Drain pasta, toss with half the bacon fat. In serving dish, layer hot pasta with crumbled farmer's cheese (túró), crispy bacon bits, and generous dollops of sour cream. Season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with chopped chives. Serve immediately. Traditional Hungarian pasta dish.

name: Halászlé
instructions: Make fish broth: simmer fish heads, tails, and bones with 2 sliced onions, salt, and water for 1 hour. Strain. Sauté finely chopped onion in oil, add 3 tbsp sweet paprika and 1 tsp hot paprika, immediately add strained broth to prevent burning. Add chopped tomato and green pepper, bring to boil. Add carp and catfish chunks, simmer 15-20 min until fish cooked. Serve hot in bowls with fresh white bread. Hungarian fisherman's soup.

name: Somlói Galuska
instructions: Cut three types of sponge cake (plain, chocolate, walnut) into small cubes. Sprinkle with rum and soak with vanilla custard. Layer in glass bowl: cake mixture, chocolate sauce, whipped cream, repeat. Top with whipped cream, dust with cocoa powder, and sprinkle with chopped walnuts and rum-soaked raisins. Chill before serving. Hungarian trifle dessert.

name: Pörkölt
instructions: Sauté 3 chopped onions in lard until golden. Remove from heat, stir in 2 tbsp sweet paprika, then add 1kg cubed beef. Return to heat, sear meat. Add chopped tomato and pepper, crushed garlic, pinch caraway seeds, salt. Add just enough water to cover. Simmer covered 2 hours until meat tender, adding water if needed. Uncover at end to thicken sauce. Serve with nokedli or bread. Hungarian beef stew, base for goulash.

name: Gundel Palacsinta
instructions: Make thin crepes. For filling: grind 200g walnuts, mix with 1/2 cup sugar, 1/4 cup rum-soaked raisins, orange zest, enough milk to make spreadable paste. Spread on crepes, fold into quarters. Place in buttered dish, warm in oven. Serve topped with warm chocolate sauce and whipped cream. Famous Gundel restaurant dessert.

name: Rakott Krumpli
instructions: Boil 1kg potatoes in skins, peel and slice. Hard-boil 4 eggs, slice. Slice 200g smoked sausage. Butter baking dish, sprinkle with breadcrumbs. Layer: potato slices, sausage, egg slices, salt, pepper, sour cream. Repeat layers, end with potato. Dot with butter, top with sour cream, sprinkle breadcrumbs. Bake at 180°C (350°F) 30-35 min until golden. Hungarian layered potato casserole.

name: Vepřo Knedlo Zelo
instructions: Roast seasoned pork shoulder with onion, caraway seeds, and water until tender and golden. Slice meat. Make gravy from pan drippings with flour and water. Stew sauerkraut with butter, pinch sugar, and caraway. Serve sliced pork with bread dumplings, sauerkraut, and gravy. Iconic Czech meal.

name: Kulajda
instructions: Sauté sliced mushrooms and diced potatoes. Add water, bay leaf, allspice, salt, boil until tender. Make slurry of cream and flour, whisk into soup, simmer. Add chopped dill and splash vinegar for sour note. Serve with poached or hard-boiled egg and dollop of sour cream. Czech creamy dill mushroom soup.

name: Škubánky
instructions: Boil potatoes, mash or rice. While warm, mix with flour (about 1/3 flour to potato ratio) and salt to make soft dough. Roll into small dumplings, boil in salted water until they float. Drain, toss with melted butter. Serve with ground poppy seeds mixed with sugar, and warm milk poured over. Czech sweet potato dumplings.

name: Bramboráky
instructions: Grate 500g potatoes, drain some liquid but keep starch. Add crushed garlic, 1 tsp marjoram, salt, pepper, 1 egg, 2-3 tbsp flour, splash milk to make thick batter. Fry spoonfuls in hot oil as thin pancakes until golden and crisp both sides. Serve hot as side or main. Czech potato pancakes.

name: Smažený Sýr
instructions: Cut cheese into 1.5 cm thick slabs. Dredge in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, repeat egg and breadcrumbs for double coating. Fry in hot oil until golden and cheese begins to melt. Serve immediately with tartar sauce, lemon wedge, and fries. Czech fried cheese.

name: Kalduny
instructions: Make dough as for pelmeni. Filling: mix ground meat with grated onion, marjoram, salt, pepper, splash of broth. Roll dough, cut circles, fill, seal in half-moon or pouch shapes. Boil in salted water. Serve with melted butter or in broth. Belarusian/Lithuanian dumplings.

name: Vereshchaka
instructions: Marinate pork ribs in beet kvass overnight with onion, garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns. Drain, reserve marinade. Brown ribs, add reserved marinade, simmer until tender. Thicken sauce with flour paste. Serve with rye bread to soak up tangy gravy. Ancient Belarusian dish.

name: Machanka
instructions: Fry pork pieces and sliced sausage. Sauté onion, sprinkle flour, add water to make gravy. Stir in sour cream, season. Serve thick meat gravy in bowl, with blini for dipping. Belarusian dipping stew served with pancakes.

name: Bulviniai Blynai
instructions: Grate potatoes and onion, squeeze liquid. Mix with egg, flour, salt. Fry spoonfuls in oil until golden and crisp. Serve hot with sour cream. Lithuanian potato pancakes (similar to draniki but often thicker).

name: Vėdarai
instructions: Grate raw potatoes, squeeze slightly. Mix with fried bacon bits, sautéed onion, salt, pepper, marjoram, and splash milk. Stuff mixture loosely into cleaned pork casings. Prick with needle, bake in oven with some fat until browned and cooked through. Slice and serve. Lithuanian potato sausage.

name: Skilandinys
instructions: Cut pork and bacon into chunks, mix with crushed garlic, salt, pepper, coriander. Stuff into cleaned pig stomach, sew closed. Press between boards under weight, cold smoke, then dry age for several weeks. Slice thinly as cold cut. Lithuanian smoked meat delicacy.

name: Cepelinai
instructions: Grate half potatoes raw, squeeze. Boil other half, mash. Combine both with salt to make dough. Form oval shape (zeppelin), stuff with seasoned ground pork and onion mixture. Boil gently until they float, then 15-20 min. Serve with sour cream and bacon-onion sauce. Lithuanian national dish.

name: Borscht with Vushka
instructions: Make clear beet broth: boil beets with onion, carrot, parsley root, strain, season with vinegar, sugar, salt. For vushka (little ears): make dough, fill with mixture of cooked chopped mushrooms, onion, breadcrumbs. Form small dumplings, boil. Serve clear borscht with vushka floating, dollop sour cream. Ukrainian Christmas Eve version.

name: Nalisniki
instructions: Make thin crepe batter. Fry crepes. For filling: mix farmer's cheese with sugar, egg yolk, vanilla. Spread on crepes, roll up. Place in buttered dish, dot with butter, bake 15 min. Serve with sour cream and berry sauce. Ukrainian cheese-filled crepes.

name: Deruny
instructions: Same as draniki but often with more flour and egg for fluffier interior. Grate potatoes and onion, mix with egg, flour, salt. Fry in oil. Serve with sour cream. Ukrainian potato pancakes.

name: Kartoplia Solomkoiu
instructions: Cut potatoes into matchstick strips. Soak in cold water, drain and dry thoroughly. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crisp. Toss with salt, paprika, garlic powder. Serve as snack. Ukrainian potato straws.

name: Lviv Syrnyk
instructions: Blend 1kg farmer's cheese until smooth. Mix with 200g softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 4 egg yolks, lemon zest, vanilla, 3 tbsp potato starch. Fold in whipped egg whites. Bake in water bath at 160°C (320°F) 1 hour until set. Cool completely, cover with chocolate glaze. Refrigerate. Lviv cheesecake.

name: Tsimes
instructions: Slice carrots, simmer with butter, honey, orange juice, and dried fruits until carrots tender and liquid syrupy. Add cinnamon. Serve warm or cold. Sweet carrot stew, traditional Ashkenazi dish.

name: Gefilte Fish
instructions: Grind fish fillets with onion. Mix with matzo meal, eggs, salt, sugar, pepper. Form oval patties. Simmer in fish broth with carrot slices, bay leaf for 1.5 hours. Cool in broth. Serve with jellied broth and beet horseradish. Traditional Jewish poached fish patties.
